decider.cite: forcing a decision when a trial ends keeps the agreement short enough to read
decider.reply_head:
Yes

The evaluation rests on evidence. The inventory counts 24 experiment lines, 14 of them expired, and none ever decided by a Decider. The pick gives each line a hypothesis, a metric with its unit, and a trial length. Its target is 0 undecided lines past their trial. Its counter-metrics are a defect after an adopt or drop, and a lost rule. The next three retros are the checkpoint.

One gap: the sign-off seat is not named. I'd have the Decider own the retro-time decision for each expired entry.

pm.cite: the agreement keeps one Experimental section
pm.reply_head:
Support-it
This fits the standing rules: it creates one short experimental section, makes every trial state a hypothesis, metric and unit, and forces a retro decision when its trial expires. That keeps accountability to evidence, stops stale experiments lingering, and preserves the product-first principle without over-specifying up front. decider.cite: the agreement short enough to read and stops expired experiments lingering
decider.reply_head:
Support-it
This proposal is framed by the retro evidence: 24 experiment lines, 14 expired by count, no prior Decider decisions, and a trial-length rule tied to a next-retro decision. It also adds a clear evidence standard (metric + unit, adoption/revise/drop decision with evidence) and preserves the existing protocol while moving only the scattered trials into one experimental section. The team has the needed seats: PM, QA, architect, developer, audit lens, Decider, agile coach, and the product
